Blood Test Reference Sheet
Educational overview of common blood tests, what they measure, and typical adult reference ranges
This sheet summarizes commonly ordered blood tests for general education (e.g., school or intro medical coursework).
Reference ranges vary between laboratories, instruments, and patient populations (age, sex, pregnancy, altitude, etc.), so treat
these as illustrative, not diagnostic. Always use the range printed on an actual lab report, since that is calibrated to the specific lab
and method used.
Complete Blood Count (CBC)
TestWhat It MeasuresTypical Adult Reference Range*
Hemoglobin (Hb)Oxygen-carrying protein in red blood cellsMen: 13.5–17.5 g/dL
Women: 12.0–15.5 g/dL
Hematocrit (Hct)Percentage of blood volume made up of red cellsMen: 41–50%
Women: 36–44%
Red Blood Cell (RBC) countNumber of red cells per volume of bloodMen: 4.5–5.9 million/μL
Women: 4.0–5.2 million/μL
White Blood Cell (WBC) countNumber of infection-fighting cells4,000–11,000 /μL
Platelet countCell fragments involved in clotting150,000–450,000 /μL
Mean Corpuscular Volume (MCV)Average size of red blood cells80–100 fL
Lipid Panel
TestWhat It MeasuresTypical Adult Reference Range*
Total CholesterolTotal cholesterol carried in the blood< 200 mg/dL desirable
LDL Cholesterol“Bad” cholesterol; builds arterial plaque< 100 mg/dL optimal
HDL Cholesterol“Good” cholesterol; helps clear LDLMen: > 40 mg/dL
Women: > 50 mg/dL
TriglyceridesFat circulating in the blood, from diet/liver< 150 mg/dL
Cardiac Enzymes / Markers
TestWhat It MeasuresTypical Adult Reference Range*
Troponin I or TProtein released when heart muscle is damaged; key marker for heart attack< 0.04 ng/mL (assay-dependent; rises within 3–6 hrs of injury)
CK-MBHeart-specific fraction of creatine kinase enzyme0–5 ng/mL (varies by lab)
BNP / NT-proBNPHormone released when heart is stretched or strained; used to assess heart failureBNP < 100 pg/mL (age/assay-dependent)
MyoglobinEarly but non-specific marker of muscle damage25–72 ng/mL (varies by lab)
Basic Metabolic Panel (selected)
TestWhat It MeasuresTypical Adult Reference Range*
Sodium (Na+)Key electrolyte for fluid balance & nerve function135–145 mmol/L
Potassium (K+)Electrolyte critical for heart rhythm & muscle function3.5–5.0 mmol/L

TestWhat It MeasuresTypical Adult Reference Range*
Glucose (fasting)Blood sugar level70–99 mg/dL
CreatinineWaste product filtered by kidneys; marker of kidney function0.6–1.3 mg/dL
*Reference ranges shown are commonly cited adult ranges for general education and can differ by laboratory, analyzer, units, age, sex, and
clinical context. This sheet is for learning purposes only and is not a substitute for an actual laboratory report or professional medical
interpretation.
